_about: Reproducibility repeats (prepared, not started): per repeat, the original's per-opponent match id, seed and seats, game dice, option-order seed, prompt, rules and settings, its coverage, today's blockers, the paid gates, cost basis, GPU plan and start commands. Written by tools/v3/repeats/repeats.py manifest from v3.db (read-only).

seed_mechanism.finding: The original runner builds have no per-pair seed field: a new pair's seed and seating come from the two player names and the rules hash (Rules::pair_seed, Rules::sides), so a renamed repeat would get other dice. The late entries' seeds are exactly that (checked for #780, #807, #818, #845, #867, #905, #920); Liquid d1-ultra's League 1 seeds are not (older rule).
seed_mechanism.used: Runner change on branch pinned-pairs, commit 4ca4f08 (Zeki #4710), run as d24d90a (branch pinned-late-reax: the originals' runner line origin/late-reax with 4ca4f08 cherry-picked; Zeki #4860, #4886): league config field pinned_pairs {opponent: {seed: u64, seat_first: bool}} for the only_pairs_of setup, stored in the new column leagues.pinned_pairs and read wherever fixtures are derived (resume, league-add and a running league keep them); league-add --pin. Every game's dice follow from the match seed and every option order from the option-order seed and the position, never from names: a test replays #808, #856, #905 and #190 under a renamed repeat and gets every game's dice and every turn's option order of the original. Each repeat's league config carries a pin for every opponent of its original.
seed_mechanism.migration: leagues.pinned_pairs is added (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN, NULL) by the new build's ensure_schema the first time it opens a database; not applied to production v3.db yet (nothing has run it there); no existing row is edited, and NULL means no pins, so older builds and every existing league are unaffected.
